messages.subject: Re: uploaded file (jpg) doesnt print
parts:
This seems to be the problematic code:



   $('body').on('change', function(e) {



      var fileList = e.target.files;



        if(fileList != undefined) {



            var file = fileList[0];



            $('#wing').attr('src', 'uploads/'+file.name);



            var canvas = document.getElementById('myCanvas');



            var context = canvas.getContext('2d');



            context.drawImage(img, 0, 0, 500, 500 * img.height / img.width) 



          }  
        });
      });

If I'm correct, this event handler will be executed (with fileList != undefined) as soon as the upload *begins*, not ends. This is too early. I could think of ways to fix this approach but I think there is a better way.

Is there a reason you need to use a canvas instead of just a regular image? It would make more sense to me to do this:
  1. Put a uiOutput("wing") where the image will appear
  2. Create a new image tag every time an upload occurs:
      output$wing <- renderUI({
        if (is.null(input$foto))
          return("Please upload a photo")
        file.copy(input$foto$datapath, paste("./www/uploads/",input$foto$name, sep=""))
        return(tags$img(src=paste("uploads/", input$foto$name, sep="")))
      })
  3. Add CSS to constrain the photo display:
      tags$style(type="text/css", "#wing img { max-width: 500px; max-height: 500px; }")
    or if you prefer to scale it to 500px width:
      tags$style(type="text/css", "#wing img { width: 500px; }")
  4. Handle the mouse movements/clicks this way:
      $(document).on("mousemove", "#wing img", function(evt) { ... });
      $(document).on("mousedown", "#wing img", function(evt) { ... });
    See "Direct and delegated events" on this page to see why this approach is superior (since the contents of #wing will be repeatedly deleted and recreated by Shiny).
Hope that gives you enough to go on...


On Thu, Apr 18, 2013 at 7:45 AM, Mart Vogel <mart....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi!

I'm making a shiny application to identify bee species based on wing morphology (landmarks) (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/martijn1987/zutalors/). I will give you a quick rundown how to tool should work eventually.

-Upload user wingpicture
-Choose which reference dataset you want to compare your unidentified specimen too
-Choose which listfile/labels should accompany your reference data (decide the taxonomical level on which you want to identify your specimen
-Place the landmarks on specific points on the wing (in the example you have to place them on the spikes of the stars (5 landmarks total!)
-Click identify me, the species name is displayed below the picture.

One problem we are still not able the fix is the uploading. When we run the tool locally, it sometimes does print the uploaded picture. But only if you have already uploaded it before. I think this is because the program tries to print it before the upload is finished. When I run it online I can't manage to get the uploaded picture at all, but some people seem to be able to. 

Does anyone have a solution for this?

ui, server and js are here: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/5413170

--
